attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post of 2026-05-18, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The draft keeps both parts of the claim: Musk was found too late, and the legitimacy of OpenAI's conduct was not decided. 'Whimper' is rhetoric and is not scored.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. 'Legitimate' is read as the substantive merits and 'procedural' as a ruling on timeliness. The trial ending does not mean appeals are exhausted.

evidence.note: KQED, same-day report: the jury accepted OpenAI's statute-of-limitations defence, so Musk was too late.
TheWrap, same-day report: the jury did not decide the merits of Musk's claims.
CBS, same-day report: unanimous advisory verdict on limitations grounds, which the judge accepted before dismissing the claims.
OpenAI's lawyer called the verdict substantive. That is a party's advocacy and does not show the jury ruled on the merits. The same article reports the finding was on limitations.

reviews.rationale: Several independent same-day reports agree. The jury found Musk's claims time-barred, the judge adopted that finding and dismissed the claims, and the jury did not rule on the merits. OpenAI counsel's 'substantive' label is advocacy and does not contradict how the case was disposed of. Retrieval dates are after the cutoff, but every article was published on 2026-05-18, so all can be used.
